title: Platelet proteome in Essential Thrombocythemia
projectDescription: Platelets from healthy donors (HD) and Essential Thrombocythemia (ET) patients were isolated from peripheral blood. The HD were treated with low dose aspirin (100mg) once daily and blood samples were collected before and after treatment. ET patients from different mutational backgrounds (JAK2 V617F, MPL W515K/L, CALR Type 1 &2) were either untreated or treated with aspirin, HU, anagrelide or a combination of them at the time of blood donation. Platelets were pelleted after centrifugation (1100rpm, no brake  at room temperature) and were snap frozen in liquid nitrogen before stored to -80C for mass spectrometry.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Platelet samples were thawed on ice and 10 volumes of lysis buffer 100mM triethylammonium bicarbonate (TEAB, Sigma), 1% SDS (Genomic Solutions) was added. Immediately samples were boiled at 95 °C and 1000 rpm for 5 minutes. After cooling to room temperature samples were sonicated in a Bioruptor (Diagenode) for 10 minutes at 30 seconds on/off cycles. An aliquot was removed for BCA protein determination (Pierce kit, Thermo Fisher Scientific). 500 µg of protein (or less if unavailable) was supplemented with lysis buffer to a final volume of 270 µl. Proteins were reduced in 5mM dithiothreitol (Sigma) for 1 hour at 50 °C and 1000 rpm followed by alkylation in 10 mM 2-chloro-acetamide (Fluka) for 45 minutes at room temperature and 1000 rpm. Proteins were precipitated after addition of 1/20 volume of 1M NaCl (Fluka) with four volumes of acetone (BioSolve) (A.M.J Crowell et al., Analytica Chimica Acta, Volume 796, 24 September 2013, Pages 48-54). Pellets were dissolved in 150 µl 100 mM TEAB, 0.5% sodium deoxycholate (SDC, Sigma-Aldrich) by sonication in a Bioruptor for 10 minutes at 30 seconds on/off cycles. Proteins were digested with 1:100 Lys-C (Wako) at 37°C and 1200 rpm for one hour followed by addition of 1:40 Trypsin (TPCK-treated, Thermo Fisher Scientific) and incubation at 37 °C and 1200 rpm overnight. Trifluoroacetic acid (Thermo Fisher Scientific) was added to a final concentration of 0.5% and SDC was pelleted by centrifugation at 13.000 rpm for 10 minutes. Supernatants were transferred to a clean tube and 20 µg protein was desalted by C18 STAGE tip purification (modified from J. Rappsilber at al., Anal Chem. 2003 Feb 1;75(3):663-70). Final 50% acetonitrile (BioSolve) eluates were dried in a SpeedVac (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and dissolved in 100 µl 2% acetonitrile, 0.5% formic acid (BioSolve). 800 ng protein was analyzed on an Orbitrap Fusion™ Lumos™ Tribrid™ Mass Spectrometer and an EASY-nLC™ 1200 System (both Thermo Fisher Scientific) basically as described before (Sap et al., Mol Cell Proteomics. 2019 Sep; 18(9): 1705–1720).
dataProcessingProtocol: Data analysis was performed using MaxQuant version 1.6.17.0 and human proteome database (Uniprot Knowledgebase, release February 2021, including isoforms) supplemented with the mutant CALR sequences. Default settings were used with methionine oxidation, acetyl (protein N-term) and phospho (serine, threonine and tyrosine) as variable modifications, cysteine carbamidomethylation as fixed modification and Trypsin/P as protease. LFQ and iBAQ data were calculated.
